questions.question: Before planning next year's promotions, the manager of Willow Creek Inn sorts three years of reservation data in the hotel's database to find which months have the lowest occupancy. The manager is using the database for

options.A: data entry.
options.B: information analysis.
options.C: email marketing.

questions.explanation: Information analysis. Sorting and filtering stored data to find patterns, such as slow months, is information analysis that supports decisions like seasonal promotions. Data entry adds records, word processing creates documents, and email marketing sends promotions.

performanceIndicator.text: Use database for information analysis

questions.question: Two bakeries offer to supply bread to Harbor House Inn. Vendor A is 5% cheaper, but its deliveries were late four times last month. Vendor B costs more but has delivered on time for a year. Why might the inn choose Vendor B?

options.A: Reliable delivery protects the guest experience
options.B: Vendor B will lower its price later
options.C: The cheapest vendor is always the best choice

questions.explanation: Reliable delivery protects the guest experience. Late bread means guests may go without breakfast items, which hurts their experience and the inn's reputation. A small price savings may not be worth the disruption. Price alone doesn't determine value, late deliveries don't cut costs, and there's no reason to expect a price drop.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate vendors' goods and services

questions.question: Which type of chart is best for showing the percentage of a hotel's guests who come from each of five regions?

options.A: Timeline
options.B: Pie chart
options.C: Scatter plot

questions.explanation: Pie chart. A pie chart shows how parts make up a whole, such as each region's share of total guests. Line graphs show changes over time, scatter plots show relationships between two variables, and timelines show events in order.

performanceIndicator.text: Display hospitality and tourism data in charts/graphs or in tables

questions.question: A wedding planner shares a weekly status report showing completed tasks, upcoming deadlines, and any issues with the couple. This report helps

options.A: replace the project budget.
options.B: set the date of the wedding.
options.C: keep stakeholders informed.

questions.explanation: Keep stakeholders informed. Regular status reports keep clients and team members informed so they can make decisions and stay confident in the plan. They don't replace budgets, remove the need for vendors, or determine the date.

performanceIndicator.text: Apply project-management tools to monitor and communicate project progress

questions.question: Which of the following is a factor that affects a hotel's evacuation procedures:

options.A: The menu in the hotel restaurant
options.B: The hotel's loyalty program
options.C: The building's layout and number of exits
options.D: The brand of televisions in guest rooms

questions.explanation: The building's layout and number of exits. Evacuation plans depend on the building's design, number and location of exits, occupancy, and the needs of guests with disabilities. Menus, televisions, and loyalty programs don't affect how people safely leave the building.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify factors affecting evacuation procedures/protocols

questions.question: Analytics show that most visitors to a resort's website leave on the booking page without reserving. What might the resort do first?

options.A: Delete the booking page
options.B: Raise room rates to offset lost bookings
options.C: Review the booking page for problems
options.D: Stop all of its online advertising

questions.explanation: Review the booking page for problems. A high exit rate on the booking page suggests something there, such as too many steps or errors, is stopping visitors. Investigating the page is the logical first step. Deleting it, cutting advertising, or raising prices would not solve the problem.

performanceIndicator.text: Use analytical tracking tools

questions.question: A server notices a guest squinting at the menu and holding it at arm's length. Which action anticipates the guest's unspoken need?

options.A: Recommending the most expensive entrée
options.B: Asking the guest to hurry and order
options.C: Taking the menu away

questions.explanation: Offering a large-print menu. The guest's behavior suggests difficulty reading the small print. Offering a large-print menu or more light solves the problem without the guest having to ask. Rushing, removing the menu, or pushing an expensive item ignores the need.

performanceIndicator.text: Anticipate unspoken customer needs

questions.question: A written report for hospitality decision makers should begin with

options.A: the author's personal opinions.
options.B: a brief summary of key findings.
options.C: a list of every data source used.
options.D: a detailed history of the industry.

questions.explanation: A brief summary of key findings. Busy managers need the main points first, so an executive summary at the start presents key findings and recommendations. Industry history and personal opinions are unnecessary, and the list of sources belongs at the end.

performanceIndicator.text: Prepare written reports for hospitality and tourism decision-making

questions.question: Which of the following should an employee do before operating a commercial dishwasher for the first time:

options.A: Read the instructions and get proper training
options.B: Guess how it works
options.C: Remove its safety guards
options.D: Use it with any cleaning chemical available

questions.explanation: Read the instructions and get proper training. Following the manufacturer's instructions and training prevents injuries and damage to equipment. Guessing, removing safety features, and using the wrong chemicals can cause accidents or harm the machine.

performanceIndicator.text: Follow instructions for use of equipment, tools, and machinery

questions.question: Customer service is a key part of a selling relationship because

options.A: it allows salespeople to ignore customers after the sale.
options.B: it replaces product knowledge.
options.C: good service encourages customers to buy again.
options.D: it eliminates the need for products.

questions.explanation: Good service encourages customers to buy again. Service before, during, and after a sale builds trust and loyalty, leading to repeat business and referrals. Ignoring customers after the sale damages the relationship, and service doesn't replace products or product knowledge.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of customer service as a component of selling relationships

questions.question: After analyzing guest surveys, a restaurant manager finds that most complaints involve slow service on weekends. A logical conclusion is that

options.A: the restaurant should close on weekdays.
options.B: the menu should be completely replaced.
options.C: guests don't care about speed.
options.D: weekend service may need to change.

questions.explanation: Weekend service may need to change. Conclusions should follow from the data. Since complaints focus on weekend speed, staffing or service processes are likely causes. The data doesn't point to the menu, contradicts the idea that speed doesn't matter, and doesn't involve weekdays.

performanceIndicator.text: Draw conclusions based on information analysis

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of using software to automate services in a restaurant:

options.A: A host keeping a paper waiting list
options.B: A server writing orders on a notepad and carrying them back
options.C: A tablet ordering system that sends orders directly to the kitchen
options.D: A manager counting cash by hand at closing

questions.explanation: A tablet ordering system that sends orders directly to the kitchen. Tablet ordering transmits orders instantly, reducing errors and speeding service. Handwritten orders, counting cash by hand, and paper waiting lists are manual processes, not automated ones.

performanceIndicator.text: Use software to automate services

questions.question: Why is promotion especially important for hospitality services?

options.A: Guests can't test the service before buying
options.B: Customers always know exactly what to expect
options.C: Services can be returned after use

questions.explanation: Guests can't test the service before buying. Because hospitality services are intangible, customers rely on photos, reviews, and messages to judge what they'll get. Promotion helps make the experience feel real before purchase. Services do change, customers often don't know what to expect, and experiences can't be returned once used.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the concept of promotion in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A guest finds that her room wasn't cleaned when she returns in the afternoon. Which response is the best example of guest recovery?

options.A: Telling her housekeeping is busy and she'll have to wait until tomorrow
options.B: Offering a refund only if she writes a complaint letter
options.C: Explaining that she should have hung a sign on the door
options.D: Apologizing, having the room cleaned right away, and offering a free drink

questions.explanation: Apologizing, having the room cleaned right away, and offering a free drink. Effective recovery acknowledges the mistake, fixes it quickly, and shows goodwill with a small gesture. Delaying, blaming the guest, or making her jump through hoops would likely turn a minor failure into a lost customer.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of guest recovery

questions.question: A workplace that includes employees of different ages, cultures, and backgrounds is said to be

options.A: diverse.
options.B: centralized.
options.C: unionized.

questions.explanation: Diverse. Workplace diversity refers to differences among employees, such as age, ethnicity, religion, and gender. Centralized describes decision making at the top, automated refers to machines doing tasks, and unionized means employees are represented by a union.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss issues associated with workplace diversity (e.g., ethnic, generational, religious, gender)

questions.question: Which revision would make this sentence more professional: "We're gonna fix the AC in your room ASAP"?

options.A: "Your room's AC is your problem."
options.B: "AC fixed ASAP!!!"
options.C: "We're gonna get somebody to fix it soon, probably."
options.D: "We will repair your room's air conditioning soon."

questions.explanation: "We will repair your room's air conditioning soon." The revised sentence uses complete words and a courteous tone suited to guest communication. The other options keep informal slang, add excessive punctuation, or are rude.

performanceIndicator.text: Edit and revise written work consistent with professional standards

questions.question: A county health inspector arrives unannounced at Harbor Seafood Shack, checks the temperature of the coolers, looks at how raw fish is stored, and gives the restaurant a score that it must post near the door. This inspection is an example of

options.A: price competition.
options.B: a sales promotion.
options.C: government regulation.

questions.explanation: Government regulation. Local health departments inspect restaurants to make sure they follow food-safety rules, which is government regulation. Promotions, loyalty programs, and price competition are business activities, not regulations.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of regulations affecting the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A Gantt chart helps project teams by

options.A: calculating employee pay for each task.
options.B: showing tasks along a timeline.
options.C: tracking inventory levels.

questions.explanation: Showing tasks along a timeline. A Gantt chart displays tasks as bars along a timeline, making it easy to see what's due and how tasks overlap. It doesn't calculate pay, record complaints, or track inventory.

performanceIndicator.text: Apply project-management tools to monitor and communicate project progress

questions.question: Personal information management software helps employees

options.A: clean guest rooms.
options.B: manage a hotel's payroll.
options.C: organize schedules and tasks.
options.D: cook food more quickly in a kitchen.

questions.explanation: Organize schedules and tasks. Personal information management applications, such as digital calendars and task lists, keep appointments, contacts, and to-dos organized. Payroll, cooking, and cleaning aren't handled by these tools.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate personal information management/productivity applications

questions.question: An internship is valuable for a student interested in hotel management because it

options.A: replaces the need for a résumé.
options.B: provides real experience and contacts.
options.C: is always paid at a manager's salary.
options.D: guarantees a management job after graduation.

questions.explanation: Provides real experience and contacts. Internships let students apply classroom knowledge, learn how hotels operate, and meet people who can help their careers. They don't guarantee jobs, replace résumés, or pay management-level salaries.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe techniques for obtaining work experience (e.g., volunteer activities, internships)

questions.question: When a customer pays for a $26.40 dinner with a $50 bill, how much change should the cashier give?
questions.explanation: $23.60. Change is the amount paid minus the total: $50.00 - $26.40 = $23.60. Counting up from $26.40 to $50.00 confirms it. $24.60 is a subtraction error, $26.40 is the bill amount, and $33.60 is not related to the transaction.

performanceIndicator.text: Process sales transactions (e.g., cash, credit, check)

questions.question: A moment of truth is

options.A: a sale that is final and can't be refunded.
options.B: the time when a business calculates its profits.
options.C: the date a business opens.
options.D: any moment a customer forms an impression.

questions.explanation: Any moment a customer forms an impression. Every contact, such as a greeting, a phone call, or a clean lobby, shapes how customers judge a business. These are moments of truth. Profit calculations, opening dates, and final sales are not customer interactions.

performanceIndicator.text: Deliver positive moments of truth

questions.question: Up-selling in a restaurant means

options.A: refusing to serve guests who order inexpensive items.
options.B: rushing guests so more tables can be seated.
options.C: adding items to a bill without asking.
options.D: suggesting a better item that adds to the experience.

questions.explanation: Suggesting a better item that adds to the experience. Up-selling offers a better or larger option, such as a premium side or a larger size, that adds value for the guest and revenue for the business. Refusing service, adding charges without consent, and rushing guests are poor practices.

performanceIndicator.text: Up-sell to enhance customer experience

questions.question: Which of the following can help a hotel maintain service standards during peak periods:

options.A: Removing amenities
options.B: Skipping room inspections
options.C: Telling guests to expect poor service

questions.explanation: Scheduling extra trained staff. Planning for busy times with enough trained staff helps the hotel deliver the same quality guests expect. Skipping inspections, cutting amenities, and lowering expectations all reduce service standards.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain service standards during peaks in demand

questions.question: Which of the following is the best approach when taking notes during a meeting:

options.A: Write key points and action items
options.B: Write notes only after the meeting ends
options.C: Avoid taking notes so you can listen
options.D: Copy everything exactly as it is said

questions.explanation: Write key points and action items. Effective note-taking captures main ideas, decisions, and tasks so they can be acted on later. Writing every word is impossible and makes it hard to listen, while not taking notes or waiting until later risks forgetting important details.

performanceIndicator.text: Utilize note-taking strategies

questions.question: Which of the following is a factor that affects customer-service practices in hospitality businesses:

options.A: Guest expectations
options.B: The age of the owner's car
options.C: The color of the parking lot
options.D: The number of windows in the building

questions.explanation: Guest expectations. Service practices are shaped by what guests expect, along with company policies, competition, and employee training. Parking lot color, window count, and the owner's car have no effect on how service is delivered.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify factors affecting customer-service practices in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Which of the following is a current trend in the hospitality and tourism industry:

options.A: Guests using mobile apps to check in and unlock rooms
options.B: Restaurants removing menu information from the internet
options.C: Airlines requiring paper tickets for all flights

questions.explanation: Guests using mobile apps to check in and unlock rooms. Mobile check-in and digital room keys let guests skip the front desk, reflecting the industry's move toward convenience and contactless service. Removing online booking, requiring paper tickets, and hiding menus online all run against current trends.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe current issues and trends in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: An HR manager at a resort is asked to hire a friend's relative who is less qualified than other applicants. What is the most ethical response?

options.A: Create a new position for the relative
options.B: Hire the most qualified applicant based on job requirements
options.C: Hire the relative to keep the friend happy
options.D: Lower the job requirements so the relative qualifies

questions.explanation: Hire the most qualified applicant based on job requirements. Ethical hiring is based on fair, job-related qualifications. Favoring a friend's relative, creating unnecessary jobs, or changing requirements to fit one person is unfair to other applicants.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of ethics in human resources management

questions.question: Which of the following should a cashier check before accepting a coupon:

options.A: The expiration date and restrictions
options.B: The weather forecast
options.C: The customer's age

questions.explanation: The expiration date and restrictions. Coupons often have expiration dates and conditions, such as one per customer or minimum purchases. Checking these ensures the discount is applied correctly. Age, weather, and competitors' prices don't determine whether a coupon is valid.

performanceIndicator.text: Process complimentary offers and coupons/discounts

questions.question: The Grandview Hotel normally charges $139 a night, but when a three-day music festival comes to town each June, it raises its rate to $289 because rooms sell out quickly. The hotel is using

options.A: price lining.
options.B: demand-based pricing.
options.C: cost-plus pricing.

questions.explanation: Demand-based pricing. Demand-based pricing raises or lowers prices based on how many customers want the service at a given time. Cost-plus pricing adds a set markup to costs, price lining offers products at a few set price points, and bundle pricing sells several services together for one price.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of price in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Anticipating unspoken customer needs means

options.A: waiting for guests to make every request.
options.B: guessing what all guests want and treating them the same.
options.C: asking guests to fill out long forms.
options.D: noticing what a guest may want before the guest asks.

questions.explanation: Noticing what a guest may want before the guest asks. Attentive employees watch for cues, such as a guest with a cold bringing extra tissues or a family with a stroller needing a ramp, and meet those needs proactively. Waiting, paperwork, and one-size-fits-all service miss individual needs.

performanceIndicator.text: Anticipate unspoken customer needs

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of technology changing the hospitality and tourism industry:

options.A: Airlines eliminating online check-in
options.B: Restaurants accepting only cash
options.C: Travelers comparing prices on booking apps
options.D: Hotels using only handwritten reservation books

questions.explanation: Travelers comparing prices on booking apps. Booking apps let travelers compare prices and reviews instantly, which has changed how businesses compete. Handwritten reservations, cash-only policies, and eliminating online check-in move away from technology rather than reflecting its impact.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain ways that technology impacts the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A busy beach-resort restaurant is understaffed during a holiday weekend. Which approach best maintains service standards?

options.A: Serve food without checking quality
options.B: Close half the tables without telling guests
options.C: Offer a simpler menu the kitchen can make well
options.D: Let guests wait without any updates

questions.explanation: Offer a simpler menu the kitchen can make well. A streamlined menu helps the kitchen keep quality and speed high under pressure. Leaving guests uninformed, skipping quality checks, and confusing seating changes all lower standards and frustrate guests.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain service standards during peaks in demand

questions.question: The growth of commercial airlines in the mid-1900s affected the tourism industry by

options.A: reducing the number of hotels in the world.
options.B: making vacations shorter.
options.C: ending the use of travel agents.
options.D: opening distant places to more travelers.

questions.explanation: Opening distant places to more travelers. Air travel opened distant destinations to ordinary travelers, which led to rapid growth in international tourism and hotel construction. It increased rather than reduced hotels, and travel agents grew in importance for decades afterward.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the development of the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Why is the hospitality and tourism industry considered a major part of many economies?

options.A: It creates jobs and brings in spending
options.B: It operates only during summer
options.C: It produces most of the world's raw materials

questions.explanation: It creates jobs and brings in spending. Tourism generates spending at hotels, restaurants, and attractions, supporting many jobs and tax revenue. It doesn't produce raw materials, operates year-round, and is one of the largest employers worldwide.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A wedding couple wants a lower price for a reception, but the venue manager can't cut the room rate. Which offer is the best example of negotiation skills?

options.A: Lower the rate below cost
options.B: Keep the rate but add a free dessert table
options.C: Tell the couple to find another venue

questions.explanation: Keep the rate but add a free dessert table. Offering added value without changing the rate meets the couple's desire for a better deal while protecting the venue's revenue. Refusing to talk, losing money, or sending the couple away doesn't reach an agreement that works for both sides.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate negotiation skills

questions.question: After a cooking class, Saffron Studio posts a short video recap on social media and tags each participant who agreed to be featured. What is the main purpose of this?

options.A: To charge participants an extra fee
options.B: To keep customers engaged after the class
options.C: To replace the need for future classes

questions.explanation: To keep customers engaged after the class. Sharing a recap keeps participants connected to the business and encourages them to book again and tell friends. It doesn't replace classes, charge fees, or collect payment data.

performanceIndicator.text: Use digital media to enhance customer post-sales experience

questions.question: Which of the following describes a role of business in society:

options.A: Providing goods, services, and jobs
options.B: Collecting income taxes
options.C: Writing the laws that regulate trade

questions.explanation: Providing goods, services, and jobs. Businesses produce the goods and services people need and create jobs and income. Governments write laws, collect taxes, and operate public schools.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of business in society

questions.question: Cliffside Inn is the only hotel in the area with an oceanfront view from every room. This feature is the inn's

options.A: fixed cost.
options.B: competitive advantage.
options.C: sales quota.

questions.explanation: Competitive advantage. A unique, valued feature that competitors can't easily copy is a competitive advantage. A fixed cost is an expense that doesn't change with sales, a sales quota is a goal, and a target market is the group of customers the inn serves.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify product's/service's competitive advantage

questions.question: A deep fryer in a restaurant kitchen has started smoking more than usual. What should the cook do?

options.A: Pour water into the oil to cool it
options.B: Unplug it and try to repair it himself
options.C: Turn it off and report it
options.D: Keep frying to finish the orders

questions.explanation: Turn it off and report it. Unusual smoke can signal overheating or a fire risk, so the fryer should be shut off and reported. Continuing to use it is dangerous, water causes hot oil to splatter violently, and untrained repairs can cause injury.

performanceIndicator.text: Follow instructions for use of equipment, tools, and machinery

questions.question: A local hotel sponsors a youth soccer league and hires students for summer jobs. These actions show that businesses can

options.A: avoid paying local and state taxes.
options.B: control local government.
options.C: eliminate competition.

questions.explanation: Strengthen their communities. Through sponsorships, jobs, and community involvement, businesses strengthen the places they operate. These actions don't reduce taxes, give control over government, or eliminate competitors.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of business in society

questions.question: Supply chain collaboration occurs when

options.A: a company keeps all its plans secret from suppliers.
options.B: each supplier competes to undercut the others.
options.C: a business buys from a new vendor every week.
options.D: supply chain partners share information and plans.

questions.explanation: Supply chain partners share information and plans. Collaboration means suppliers, manufacturers, and buyers share forecasts and plans, which reduces waste, delays, and costs for everyone. Secrecy, constant undercutting, and frequently switching vendors prevent the trust collaboration requires.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the benefits of supply chain collaboration

questions.question: A restaurant manager notices that several steaks were sent back for being undercooked. Which quality control action would best address the problem?

options.A: Offer guests a larger portion
options.B: Tell servers to stop taking complaints
options.C: Have cooks use a thermometer on each steak

questions.explanation: Have cooks use a thermometer on each steak. Using a thermometer measures doneness consistently, which prevents undercooked orders and protects food safety. Dropping the item, ignoring complaints, or serving larger portions doesn't fix the cooking process.

performanceIndicator.text: Utilize quality control methods at work

questions.question: Xavier is taking notes during a training session on a new reservation system. Which strategy will help him use the notes later?

options.A: Organizing notes under headings for each topic
options.B: Writing on random scraps of paper
options.C: Leaving out the steps he finds hard
options.D: Using abbreviations only he can't remember

questions.explanation: Organizing notes under headings for each topic. Headings group related information so it's easy to find and review. Scattered scraps get lost, confusing abbreviations make notes useless, and skipping difficult steps leaves out the information he'll need most.

performanceIndicator.text: Utilize note-taking strategies

questions.question: Customer service in the hospitality industry is especially important because

options.A: service is a major part of what guests buy.
options.B: guests can easily return a bad experience.
options.C: prices are the same at every business.

questions.explanation: Service is a major part of what guests buy. In hospitality, how guests are treated is part of the product. A meal or a hotel stay is judged largely by the service. Guests interact constantly with employees, experiences can't be returned, and prices vary widely.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of customer service in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following helps prevent credit card fraud at a hotel front desk:

options.A: Writing card numbers on the registration form
options.B: Accepting any card without checking
options.C: Keeping cards for guests during their stay
options.D: Comparing the name on the card with the guest's ID

questions.explanation: Comparing the name on the card with the guest's ID. Verifying that the card matches the guest's identification helps confirm the cardholder is present. Writing down card numbers creates theft risks, accepting cards without checking invites fraud, and holding guests' cards is improper.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify credit card fraud prevention methods

questions.question: Placing quotation marks around a phrase when searching online helps the user

options.A: search only images.
options.B: find that exact phrase.
options.C: translate the results.

questions.explanation: Find that exact phrase. Quotation marks tell the search engine to look for the words together in that order, which narrows results. They don't limit results to images, block ads, or translate pages. Those require other tools or settings.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic web-search skills

questions.question: Which of the following should a project manager do when a project falls behind schedule:

options.A: Hide the delay from stakeholders
options.B: Ignore the delay and hope it resolves
options.C: Find the cause and correct it

questions.explanation: Find the cause and correct it. Monitoring a project means comparing progress with the plan and acting when problems appear, such as adding resources or adjusting tasks. Ignoring delays, overreacting by canceling, or hiding problems lead to bigger issues.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor projects and take corrective actions

questions.question: Dividing hospitality customers into groups such as business travelers, families, and retirees is called

options.A: price fixing.
options.B: market segmentation.
options.C: mass marketing.

questions.explanation: Market segmentation. Market segmentation splits a market into groups with similar needs so a business can tailor its offerings and promotions. Market saturation means a market can't absorb more products, price fixing is an illegal agreement among competitors, and mass marketing targets everyone the same way.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify ways to segment hospitality and tourism markets

questions.question: Information that a hospitality business collects directly for a specific purpose, such as a survey of its guests, is

options.A: historical data.
options.B: primary information.
options.C: syndicated research.

questions.explanation: Primary information. Primary information is gathered firsthand for the business's own needs. Secondary information already exists from another source, historical data is past records, and syndicated research is collected by outside firms and sold to many clients.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of primary hospitality and tourism market information
